newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks expected to open mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks expected to open mixed to higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to higher with investors pinning their hopes on a resumption of strength in the high tech sector.

"We're back to the techs," said Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities. "When they began to firm late in the day yesterday, the market went up. If they take a hit today then we'll probably head lower again."
In the absence of fresh economic data, investors will be waiting to see how today's Treasury auction of $12 billion in 10-year notes affects the bond market.
"The results of the auction will be the market mover for bonds today," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Bond market players will also be watching for the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's January index on area manufacturing.

Cardillo said investors will remain nervous about AMR Corp and airline stocks in general. Negotiations between AMR's American Airlines and the union representing its pilots recessed late Tuesday night without an agreement that would avert a strike at midnight Friday against the No. 2 U.S. carrier.
"The sectors that I really do not favor at this point are the airlines, because of the AMR situation, and the oil group," Cardillo said.

"Prices have settled down in the crude oil group, and I have a feeling the next sector to see a sell-off will be the oil stocks," he said. "What is now happening in the tech group will take hold in energy stocks."
He said techs would be closely watched today.
"The sell-off in the techs should be viewed as healthy as it is not causing the rest of the market to disintegrate," he said.
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average was up 228.79 points, or 1.26 percent, at 18,520.76.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was off 2.8 points at 4301.5.
U.S. shares in London were higher across the board, with high techs leading the way. Intel Corp was up 3/4 at 152-1/2 while International Business Machines Corp was up 1/2 at 145-1/4.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly lower, with the long bond down 5/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
The dollar hit a 34-month high against the yen in Tokyo and hovered above 1.68 marks in Europe.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column discusses Ugly Duckling Corp, which finances its own sales of used cars to individuals with troubled credit or employment histories. It said the company sold five million shares Monday at $18.625 each.

The New York Times's Market Place column says Chevron Corp's $700 million investment in the Tengiz oil fields of Kazakhstan is paying off. The company is expected to tell analysts today that it made more than $80 million from the project last year, the column said.
